# odyssey-082 — review, pass 1 (Odyssey 17.1–100)

Reviewer pass 1. `gloss.json` does not exist yet; the parses of the novel forms (`novel-forms.json`) are for the second pass. `t` was not touched: the units' `t` joined reproduce the packet's 100 lines word for word, every `ln` is the line of the unit's first word, every `\n` in `t` falls on a line end, and `l` has one line per line of `t`. `p` stands on exactly the twelve units that open a Murray paragraph (17.1, 6, 16, 26, 31, 36, 41, 57, 61, 75, 77, 84). No line is flagged for scansion (packet: none), so no hand scan was owed and no irregularity note was added.

## Checks that came out clean (no change)

- Speech boundaries and quotation marks: “ opens and ” closes Telemachus 17.6–15, Odysseus 17.17–25, Penelope 17.41–44 (the speech runs across the units at 17.41, 41 and 44, “ only on the first and ” only on the last), Telemachus 17.46–56, Peiraeus 17.75–76, Telemachus 17.78–83. `mark` stands on the first unit of each of these six speeches (after the move noted above). The unit at 17.100 ends with the introduction and opens no quotation; the speech at 17.101 begins in the next part. The last unit of odyssey-081 (16.480–481) closes a meal and leaves no speech open, so nothing runs on into this part.
- 17.41 `ἦλθες, Τηλέμαχε, γλυκερὸν φάος.` and 17.41–42 `οὔ σ’ ἔτ’ ἐγώ γε / ὄψεσθαι ἐφάμην, ἐπεὶ ᾤχεο νηῒ Πύλονδε`: `l` and `i` identical to odyssey-077 (16.23, 16.23–24): “You have come, Telemachus, sweet light.” / “my sweet light.”, and the two `l` lines and the `i` clause as published. Kept.

## Findings refused

1. **17.88–89 δμῳαί kept as "slave-women" (`l`) / "serving-women" (`i`)** (the drafter's flagged item). The table row δμῶες / δμῳαί (6.69) says "maidservants" / "maids", and the parts shipped after the table (odyssey-027, -031, -037, -062, -071, -072, -076, -077, -080) follow it. But 17.88–89 are the very lines 4.49–50 shipped in odyssey-014 as "slave-women" / "serving-women", and conventions.md says a repeated line gets the same English every time (first ratified rendering wins); the table itself keeps the old English in an identical shipped line (row πέλω-root ἀμφίπολοι, 10.349: "handmaids … kept as shipped in the identical 2.136 unit"). The unit at 17.88 differs from the whole of 4.49–51 only in its last line, so the validator does not bind it, but the repetition is the point. Policy: identical shipped line keeps its words; every other δμῳαί follows the table. So 17.34 was changed to "maidservants" / "maids" (see table above), 17.88–89 left, and one sentence added to the note at 17.88 saying so.
2. **17.63 punctuation**: t ends `Ἀθήνη·` (ano teleia) but the English ends ".", as in the shipped 2.12. Left, because it reuses the shipped English whole and the next unit opens with a capital ("And at him …"), which a semicolon would make wrong. (17.64 and 17.95, where t ends with a full stop and the English had a semicolon before a capitalised unit, were changed; see the table.)
3. **17.22 `ἀλλ’ ἔρχευ·` `i` "But go on;"** against `l` "But go;". "Go on" is an idiom for "proceed", the sense of the Greek imperative; no table row.
4. **17.57 ἄπτερος "wingless"**. Considered "unwinged", "fell flat", "without effect": all pick a reading. No table row or shipped use exists; the literal word was kept and the note now states that the Greek does not say whose speech is meant. The `i` "the speech was wingless" kept.
5. **17.97 ἠλάκατα "yarn"**. Checked against odyssey-027.52, -029.305, -030.103: "yarn" in `l` and `i`. Kept; only στρωφῶσα was changed ("turning" in `l`, as shipped).
6. **17.2 `ὑπὸ ποσσὶν ἐδήσατο`**: "bound … under his feet" with "indeed, thereupon" for δὴ τότ’ ἔπειτ’ — checked against the shipped 2.4 and 15.550; kept (the published lines differ in Greek).
7. **17.4 ὅ οἱ παλάμηφιν ἀρήρει** note "pluperfect … 'had been fitted' and so 'fitted'": ἀρήρει is the pluperfect of ἄρηρα and the English "fitted" is the intransitive sense; label true, kept.
8. **17.6 ὄψεται** `l` "may see" with note "future indicative or short-vowel subjunctive": known-forms says fut. 3 sg.; the note states both readings and the purpose-clause sense; kept.
9. **17.12–13 ἔχοντά περ** note on περ "although": the note says it can mean 'although' and chooses 'as I do'; true and hedged. Kept.
10. **17.33 `τὸν μέν … Πείραιον δέ sets the two against each other`**: loose but true (the stranger and Peiraeus as the two objects of Telemachus' arrangements). Kept.
11. **17.75–76 note "the next line gives the reason"**: both lines are in this unit and line 76 is the next line; true. Kept.
12. **17.79 `δάσωνται` "from δαίομαι"**: LSJ lists δάσσασθαι under δαίομαι/δατέομαι; label acceptable; left for the second pass with gloss.json.
13. **17.12 ἀνέχεσθαι "put up with"** against the shipped "endure" (odyssey-079.274): different line and construction; "put up with" is already shipped at odyssey-030.32. Kept.
14. **17.31–33 `i` "went straight to him"**: "to him" is implied by ἀμφὶ δ’ ἄρ’ ἄλλαι … ἠγερέθοντο in the next line; kept.
15. **17.36 `i` "Then circumspect Penelope"** for `ἡ δ’`: "Then" renders δέ as a transition; kept, as in the shipped "Then prudent Telemachus …" formulas.
16. **Drafter's remaining flagged items**: 17.44 blended English — accepted and fixed (table above); 17.41 and 17.93b — verified identical, no change; ἠλάκατα — see 5; φάτ’ — decided and changed (17.25); ἄπτερος μῦθος — see 4; δμῳαί — see 1.

# Pass 2 (reviewer, second pass; `gloss.json` now read)

`t` was not touched (the units' `t` are identical to the file as pass 1 left it). Every note label, positional claim and cross-reference was re-checked against the line after pass 1's edits (every "line N" in every note was looked up; all are true), Greek → `l` → `i` was re-read unit by unit, the quotation marks were re-checked (“ on the first unit and ” on the last unit of each of the six speeches 17.6–15, 17–25, 41–44, 46–56, 75–76, 78–83; `mark` on the first unit of each; no speech runs on from or into the neighbouring part), and every `gloss.json` entry was parsed against every line where its form occurs. All 60 novel forms have an entry; no entry is over 229 characters (longest 169 outside `__broaden__`), none has an ASCII apostrophe or a line number or "here"; no key duplicates an existing glossary key. Every `__broaden__` value was checked against `odyssey-glossary.json` in the repository root: each is the old entry whole, plus ` · `, plus a new reading, and each new reading is true of the line cited. The list of forms in the part was run against the glossary: every form has an entry, and the existing entry was read for every function word and every form whose reading could differ (κατά, ἔνι, ἵνα, ἐπί, πρός, ποτί, τόν/τήν/τῷ/τῇ, ἄγ’/ἄγε, φάτ’, ἔστιν, ἦ, τοι, περ, μή, πρίν, ὄφρα and others); two missed broadenings were found (below).

**Counts of changes (Pass 2): high 1, medium 10, low 24 (total 35 rows).**

## Findings refused in pass 2

1. **17.69 `i` "companions of his father's day"** (considered: the Greek says only πατρώϊοι, "of the father"). Refused: conventions.md row πατρώιος ἑταῖρος / πατρώιοι ἑταῖροι fixes `i` "a companion of his father's day" and `l` "his father's own companions"; the unit follows the table. (The new-renderings row stays as it is.)
2. **κατά (flagged by the glosser)**: no broadening. The existing entries κατά ("down, throughout, in; + acc.") and κατ’ ("down from, throughout; + gen./acc.") cover κατὰ πτόλιν … κατ’ ἀγροὺς ("throughout", 17.18) and κατὰ κλισμούς (17.85); the tmesis in κατ-έθεντο is not a separate use of the preposition.
3. **ὄτρυνον**: the entry's second reading (impf. 1 sg. or 3 pl.) is true of the form and does not occur in this part, but it is a genuine homograph of the same -ον ending; kept (the part's use, aor. imper. 2 sg., is the first reading).
4. **ἐξερέεινον, κύνεον**: parses (impf. 3 pl., unaugmented) are true of the lines; no 1 sg. homograph is added because it occurs nowhere in the part.
5. **ἄλγιον (known entry: "comparative adv. … used absolutely")** against the note "comparative of the adjective" at 17.14: the shipped entry's gloss "all the more painful" covers this use; a broadening would only relabel the part of speech; left.
6. **ὑφορβός remark in new-renderings.md (συβώτης row)**: pipeline record, not a note; the table row it follows is real. Kept.
7. **ASCII ' for English glosses in notes**: pass 1's notes use ASCII quotes; odyssey-076 and -077 do the same or mix (-077 uses ‘ ’ in places); the validator checks `t` only and the notes' convention is "single quotes". Not changed (only `l`, `i` and glossary entries, where the shipped files print ’, were corrected).
8. **17.19–25 φάτ’ "he said" inside Odysseus' own speech**: the English "he said" with the speaker unnamed is pass 1's decision (the unaugmented φάτο is the parse the glossary already carries); the note now says another parse exists and the Greek does not name the speaker. No change to `l`/`i`.
9. **17.84 ταλαπείριος note "translated though the stranger has only just come"**: awkward but true (the epithet is rendered every time); kept.
